newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Nampak H1 earnings to disappoint.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Nampak H1 earnings to disappoint.

text.p: Nampak Ltd, South Africa's biggest packaging company, will likely post disappointing half year earnings growth, constrained by weak consumer spending and a levelling off in the economy, analysts said on Friday.
Nampak is due to report results for the six months to end-March on Monday.

At its year-end results released last November the group said it expected to build on a 14.9 percent rise in attributable earnings to 526.6 million rand, mainly on the back of capital expenditure in the last two years and productivity improvements.
But chairman Brian Connellan cautioned at the time that consumer demand growth was expected to remain low and margins had been pressured by sharp rises in raw material input costs.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast half year earnings per share improving only slightly to a consensus 58 cents from 52.2 cents in the comparable period a year ago -- a slim rise of 11 percent.
They expected the dividend a touch higher at 14.7 cents from 13.7 cents previously.
"Earnings growth is expected to be pretty bad with these interims and only around 12 percent for the full year," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
He expected growth to come in at just under 18 percent next year and said the group would probably perform below most of the packaging sector.

Nampak's dominant position in the sector was seen threatened by the emergence of recently unbundled conglomerate, Malbak Ltd, as a focused packaging firm with heavyweight industrial, the Rembrandt Group Ltd, a shareholder.
Following the unbundling, Malbak's major assets are a 68 percent stake in South African packaging firm Kohler Ltd, a 64 percent interest in London-listed MY Holdings Plc and 100 million rand in cash.
"You've got an emerging diversified packaging group which is not ideal as Nampak is highly dominant at the moment," one analyst said.
Nampak was seen currently battling to get into growth areas and hampered by weak consumer demand which was expected to continue for the rest of the year.
"The point really is that they are so big at the moment that they haven't really managed to take advantage of the fact that they've got such a good market share," one said.
